races.title: State Senate, District 5
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Kandie D. Smith
cands.bio: Democratic state senator for District 5 (Pitt and Edgecombe counties) since 2023. Earlier served in the NC House, District 8 (2019–2023). Was Greenville's first Black woman mayor and a city councilwoman from 2009. Works as a consultant. Sociology degree, Charleston Southern University, 1991.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed by Ballotpedia among her 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations.

cands.gaps: We found no documented stances from Smith on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration enforcement or H-1B, police pay, gun laws, or school vouchers and teacher pay. We did not find where she grew up or when she moved to North Carolina. We found no news reports on controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements beyond the Sierra Club. She says she backs full funding for public schools, but that is not a documented position on school choice. She says she supports affordable housing and responsible economic development, but she is not on record about specific growth or land-use policies.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Four years in the NC House (2019–2023) and the NC Senate since 2023. Before that, she was Greenville's first Black woman mayor and a city councilwoman from 2009. She currently chairs the NC Legislative Black Caucus and works as a consultant.
qual.why: Years of legislative service in both chambers plus local executive and council experience fit a job of writing law and the state budget. Committee assignments were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Years of legislative service in both chambers plus local executive and council experience fit a job of writing law and the state budget. Committee assignments were not counted toward the score.

pro-life.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, she listed abortion access among the public policy areas she is personally passionate about.

cands.name: Henry Hostetler
cands.bio: Republican candidate for NC Senate District 5 (Pitt and Edgecombe counties). Ran Baywood Racquet Club in Greenville for 26 years and worked 13 years for the Greenville Recreation and Parks Department. Past president of the NC Tennis Association and NC Tennis Foundation. Has held no elected office.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace. We found no recorded positions from him on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay. His platform only supports continued cuts to the state income tax, and he did not fill out Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2024 or 2026. His site has an endorsements page, but its contents were not available to us. Ballotpedia lists only a voter-guide group, "Peadens (Sway voting group by Mecie)," as an endorsement for 2026, and we could not tell how notable it is. We found no news coverage or controversies about him. He has held no office, so there is no voting record.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he grew up in Raeford (Hoke County), NC, and has lived in Pitt County since 1980; his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Owned and ran Baywood Racquet Club for about 26 years, after 13 years with the City of Greenville Recreation and Parks Department. Led the NC Tennis Association and Foundation. He has no legislative service and no budget or policy career on record.
qual.why: Long business ownership and management, plus city government employment, put him in the middle band. He has no prior elected or legislative experience, and the tennis association and foundation roles are nonprofit leadership, which adds nothing to the score.
